# Philosophical audit

Verdict: publishable philosophical architecture with a precise formal core,
provided novelty is presented as synthesis and methodology rather than a new
general mathematics of representation.

| Question | Audit result |
|---|---|
| Does the paper merely endorse pluralism? | no; it supplies property-relative certificate fields, quantifier domains, and falsifying examples |
| Is “information” fundamental by stipulation? | no; Section 2.5 makes the term dispensable unless bearer, equivalence, accessibility, and dynamics are identified |
| Is one ontology inferred from the calculus? | no; structural, relational-event, pragmatist, and substantival readings remain live |
| Are gauge redundancy and theoretical equivalence conflated? | no; quotient, exact equivalence, local chart, and reconstruction are separated |
| Is duality treated as ordinary approximation? | no; dual equivalence and property-relative one-way recovery are distinguished |
| Is RG reduced to generic coarse graining? | no; the discussion is qualified by the technical construction and tracked properties |
| Is structural realism represented fairly? | yes; epistemic/ontic and higher-structure concerns are acknowledged |
| Is regress from representations of representations answered? | yes; the stopping rule is inferential sufficiency for the target claim, not a metaphysical terminal language |
| Does the formalism constrain scientific practice? | yes; it requires separate completeness, positivity, uniformity, normalization, and limit-order obligations |

Strongest objection: any proof can be redescribed as a dependency graph, so the
calculus risks terminological relabeling. The paper's answer is appropriately
limited: composition alone is bookkeeping, while the recovery theorem and
countermodels show that the bookkeeping exposes noninterchangeable premises
that ordinary “same physics” language can hide.

Literature coverage spans structural realism, gauge representation and surplus
structure, duality and perspectivism, EFT/RG interpretation, relational
observables, institution-style semantics, locally covariant QFT, and OS
reconstruction. The exact phrase “representational dynamics” has substantial
usage outside this project; the manuscript therefore uses the qualified phrase
“proof-bearing representational dynamics” and makes no priority claim.
